title: Parity captures panel_row but never asserts it; devices actually end on different rows
detail: check_scenario compares only hash streams and command logs; check_states asserts only panel_open. Mouse/pad end with panel_row=1 (Down/Dpad_Down), touch ends row=0 (row-0 tap) — end input-state diverges and nothing checks it, despite the 'identical end input-state' comment.
recommended_fix: Either assert cross-device panel_row equality in the settings-panel check_states case, or drop the captured field; alternatively make every device script end on the same row so the claim is true.

title: palcheck picks the 40 vs 48 threshold by color-value equality instead of pair identity
detail: Pair class (signal vs map) is inferred from whether the pair's first color happens to equal a current map-token value. A future signal token equal to a map color silently gets the looser 40 threshold; the Python deriver classifies pairs explicitly by construction.
recommended_fix: Carry the threshold with the pair when appending (e.g. append {a, b, T_MAP} tuples like the Python pair_list) instead of value-matching pr[0] against map tokens.

title: Separation oracle has no negative-control leg — a broken cvd_simulate passes silently
evidence:
pairs: [dynamic][2]rl.Color
	defer delete(pairs)
	append(&pairs, [2]rl.Color{p.state_healthy, p.state_congested})
	append(&pairs, [2]rl.Color{p.state_healthy, p.state_critical})
detail: Every appended pair is a real palette pair expected to pass; nothing known-bad is pushed through the check. If the Machado matrices or sRGB transforms regressed (e.g. to identity), all distances grow and every leg stays green — the briefing's 'verify it bites' is not self-checking.
recommended_fix: Add a canary: append one synthetic near-identical pair and assert it FAILS the threshold (or assert the oracle's fail path fires on a rigged table), so a vacuous oracle cannot go green.
